- Overestimate prices after bullish sentiment spikes, especially when supply net is negative and events are frequent.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish and supply net is negative, particularly after recent auction events.  
- Avoid flat forecasts in the face of strong sentiment swings; adjust slope upward if sentiment is bullish and downward if bearish.  
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) often overcorrect; model should anticipate momentum shifts from sentiment history.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 75→80) — cap forecast growth to 1–2% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce slope; if below, increase.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, forecast should not rise above 10% above recent peak.  
- For auctions with high supply net, reduce forecast growth by 15–20% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
